skills.name: miso
skills.description: Routes plain-language engineering requests to MisoStack skills and workflows. Use miso to investigate, design, specify, build, review, verify, or explain work without remembering sub-skill names.

skills.name: miso-author
skills.description: Creates or improves compact skills from stated requirements and evaluated examples. Use for skill authoring or capturing an explicitly stated working preference.

skills.name: miso-automate
skills.description: Designs bounded engineering routines and handles issue reports with reproduction evidence. Use when drafting a recurring check, triaging a report, or automating a proven workflow.

skills.name: miso-debug
skills.description: Diagnoses bugs and performance regressions with a reproducible failure and controlled experiments. Use for broken, intermittent, or unexpectedly slow behavior.

skills.name: miso-design
skills.description: Designs interfaces from usage and tests architectural choices with prototypes. Use when creating a subsystem, changing ownership, or comparing substantial designs.

skills.name: miso-docs
skills.description: Writes and verifies technical documentation in Simplified Technical English. Use for tutorials, how-to guides, references, explanations, READMEs, or documentation reviews.

skills.name: miso-eval
skills.description: Evaluates skill behavior with sandbox tasks and explicit grading criteria. Use when testing prompts, skill changes, routing, or harness compatibility.

skills.name: miso-garden
skills.description: Maintains codebase structure and turns recurring defects into enforced constraints. Use for codebase gardening, repeated helpers, growing suppressions, architecture drift, or installing anti-slop checks.

skills.name: miso-loop
skills.description: Repeats a scoped task with verification until it succeeds or reaches a stop condition. Use for a bounded build-test-fix loop, a Ralph-style loop, or resuming and cancelling repeated work.

skills.name: miso-merge
skills.description: Resolves an existing Git merge or rebase conflict by preserving the intent of both changes. Use for conflicted files or a stopped merge/rebase, not to start a new merge or publish code.

skills.name: miso-perf
skills.description: Measures and improves latency, throughput, memory, or startup behavior. Use for performance improvements, profiling, benchmark design, or repeated optimization experiments.

skills.name: miso-plan
skills.description: Creates and runs dependency-aware plans with proof for each task. Use for multi-phase work, migrations, orchestration, or a task that has no existing playbook.

skills.name: miso-reflect
skills.description: Turns observed workflow failures into targeted improvements. Use when the user asks to reflect, review a session, or improve an existing skill.

skills.name: miso-research
skills.description: Traces behavior, decision history, and relevant prior work. Use when investigating how or why something works, recalling project context, or explaining a system.

skills.name: miso-review
skills.description: Reviews correctness, security, change impact, and code quality against evidence. Use for code review, adversarial review, blast-radius analysis, or final quality checks.

skills.name: miso-setup
skills.description: Checks MisoStack discovery and host capabilities without choosing fixed models. Use when installing MisoStack, diagnosing skill loading, or configuring a project.

skills.name: miso-spec
skills.description: Turns the conversation and repository evidence into a scoped specification with acceptance checks. Use when the user asks for a spec, requirements, or a written definition of what to build.

skills.name: miso-swarm
skills.description: Coordinates bounded independent work and verifies returned artifacts. Use when parallel research, coverage partitions, or candidate races are requested.

skills.name: miso-tdd
skills.description: Uses a failing behavioral test to guide a small implementation change. Use when TDD is requested or a bug has a practical regression-test path.

skills.name: miso-tickets
skills.description: Splits an agreed spec or plan into small verifiable tickets with explicit blockers. Use for breaking work into issues or preparing a backlog, with local files or an authorized tracker.

skills.name: miso-trail
skills.description: Keeps a concise evidence-backed decision trail for long work. Use for unattended runs, migrations, or an auditable handoff.

skills.name: miso-verify
skills.description: Runs, creates, or maintains project-specific verification tools and feature maps. Use when proving a change works, creating a control skill, or auditing verification coverage.

workflows.title: Investigate a question
workflows.trigger: Explain a mechanism, establish a cause, or compare evidence.
workflows.proof: Cited code or recorded observations answer the question; unknowns are explicit.

workflows.title: Fix a defect
workflows.trigger: Reproduce and repair incorrect behavior.
workflows.proof: The original failing path now passes, with before-and-after evidence.

workflows.title: Build a feature
workflows.trigger: Add or change user-visible behavior.
workflows.proof: The acceptance journey runs on the real artifact, including a relevant failure path.

workflows.title: Compare prototypes
workflows.trigger: Resolve a design or behavioral uncertainty with executable alternatives.
workflows.proof: Comparable observations support the chosen design or explicitly show an unresolved result.

workflows.title: Refactor safely
workflows.trigger: Change structure while preserving the agreed behavior.
workflows.proof: The same observable contracts hold before and after the structural change.

workflows.title: Improve performance
workflows.trigger: Fix a specific measured performance problem.
workflows.proof: Comparable samples show an improvement without violating correctness.

workflows.title: Plan verified work
workflows.trigger: Split a multi-phase change into dependent, checkable units.
workflows.proof: The plan is valid and each completed task has evidence; the final integration is checked separately.

workflows.title: Write documentation
workflows.trigger: Create or correct a tutorial, how-to, reference, or explanation.
workflows.proof: A reader can follow the documented procedure and obtain the stated result.

workflows.title: Improve a metric repeatedly
workflows.trigger: Run a bounded series of measured experiments.
workflows.proof: Each accepted experiment has comparable measurements and the final result passes correctness checks.

workflows.title: Diagnose a live runtime
workflows.trigger: Investigate leaks, CPU use, or intermittent behavior without assuming a fix.
workflows.proof: Captured runtime observations support the diagnosed mechanism or a bounded set of hypotheses.

workflows.title: Analyze a captured trace
workflows.trigger: Explain a profile, trace, heap snapshot, or crash artifact.
workflows.proof: The diagnosis points to concrete trace events and states capture limitations.

workflows.title: Verify visual equivalence
workflows.trigger: Compare two UI implementations under matched conditions.
workflows.proof: The agreed state matrix matches the baseline within declared tolerances.

workflows.title: Author a skill
workflows.trigger: Create or change a skill and prove its behavior.
workflows.proof: The skill loads and produces the intended behavior on representative sandbox cases.

workflows.title: Evaluate agent behavior
workflows.trigger: Measure a prompt or skill change against explicit cases.
workflows.proof: Recorded cases and artifacts support each evaluation verdict.

workflows.title: Bring a PR to review readiness
workflows.trigger: Resolve CI failures, review findings, or conflicts on an existing PR.
workflows.proof: Readiness is established for the current PR revision; merge remains a separate action.

workflows.title: Prepare and ship an approved change
workflows.trigger: Verify a release or merge candidate before an authorized external action.
workflows.proof: The exact candidate is verified and the remote outcome is confirmed only if an authorized action ran.

workflows.title: Run until a defined outcome
workflows.trigger: Execute one long task while the user is away.
workflows.proof: The declared outcome has evidence, or remaining blockers and exact next steps are documented.

workflows.title: Coordinate a multi-phase program
workflows.trigger: Own dependent tasks across sessions or workers.
workflows.proof: Task ownership and dependency order are valid, and integrated artifacts pass their declared checks.

workflows.title: Process an independent work queue
workflows.trigger: Build and verify independent changes with explicit publication gates.
workflows.proof: Each queue item has independent proof and external effects remain within explicit authority.

workflows.title: Build a stack for later landing
workflows.trigger: Prepare an ordered sequence of dependent changes.
workflows.proof: Each unit and the combined tip are verified, with a clear dependency order.

workflows.title: Resume prior work
workflows.trigger: Continue from a handoff or prior task state.
workflows.proof: The resumed state is reconciled against current artifacts rather than accepted from a prior summary.

workflows.title: Pause with a usable handoff
workflows.trigger: Suspend work without losing state or proof.
workflows.proof: A new session can identify current state and resume without reconstructing lost context.

workflows.title: Audit local runtime leftovers
workflows.trigger: Inspect worktrees or simulator resources before approved cleanup.
workflows.proof: The candidate list is justified; any deletion has scoped approval and a verified outcome.

workflows.title: Prepare a focused pull request
workflows.trigger: Package an authorized change for review.
workflows.proof: The review package accurately describes the full change and its executed checks.
